applied.entry: PRIMERS cat Business of the Sommelier, trap 3
applied.old: Price the glass from the wholesale cost, not from the bottle's list price.
applied.new: Two glass sums are examined: the classic rule prices one glass at the bottle's wholesale cost, while the Court's BTG costing starts from the bottle's list price, divided by 25 oz (750 ml) and multiplied by the pour, so a bottle listed at $100 gives a 5 oz glass at $20.
applied.claim: A by the glass figure is worked from the bottle's wholesale cost and never from its list price.
applied.verification: verified against the Court's own cell, no search spent: .scripts/cms/subjects/business-of-the-sommelier.json, row Calculations - BTG Costing, quotes page 93 as 'BTG Cost = (Bottle List Price/25oz/750ml) * oz/ml pour'; the wholesale rule kept as the classic convention, the Court's formula taught beside it
applied.source: CMS-A curriculum guide (8.2023), page 93, row Calculations - BTG Costing

applied.entry: PRIMERS cat Italy Central & South, fact Chianti
applied.old: A separate and larger DOCG around the Classico zone, at least 70 per cent Sangiovese, with subzones such as Rufina and Colli Senesi.
applied.new: A separate and larger DOCG around the Classico zone. Sangiovese: at least 70 per cent, the figure the Court prints and the rule for earlier vintages, lowered to 60 per cent from the 2026/27 harvest campaign by the rules amended in June 2026. Its subzones, such as Rufina and Colli Senesi, number eight since Terre di Vinci was added in 2026.
applied.claim: Chianti DOCG requires at least 70 per cent Sangiovese.
applied.verification: high, applied as written; agrees with the tuscany article (law, tiers; places); the Court's printed 70 kept beside the new figure
applied.source: Chianti DOCG disciplinare as amended, Gazzetta Ufficiale 13 June 2026; gamberorosso.it, 16 June 2026
